scope: Eight PubMed-indexed articles across the eight requested specialties. Reference values below are explicit PubMed abstract facts, not an independent clinician's assessment.
source_verification: Each exact PubMed record was opened; PMID/title and DOI when present were checked against the record. Publication types are recorded only when visible in the record. Abstract sentences are quoted verbatim.

cases.title: Empagliflozin in Heart Failure with a Preserved Ejection Fraction
cases.record_status: PubMed record identity confirmed; abstract-level claims not clinically independently validated.
cases.population: Patients with class II-IV heart failure and ejection fraction >40%.
cases.total_n_sentence: In this double-blind trial, we randomly assigned 5988 patients with class II-IV heart failure and an ejection fraction of more than 40% to receive empagliflozin (10 mg once daily) or placebo, in addition to usual therapy.

outcomes.outcome: composite cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure
outcomes.source_sentence: Over a median of 26.2 months, a primary outcome event occurred in 415 of 2997 patients (13.8%) in the empagliflozin group and in 511 of 2991 patients (17.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.69 to 0.90; P<0.001).

outcomes.outcome: total number of hospitalizations for heart failure
outcomes.source_sentence: The total number of hospitalizations for heart failure was lower in the empagliflozin group than in the placebo group (407 with empagliflozin and 541 with placebo; hazard ratio, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.61 to 0.88; P<0.001).

cases.study_relationship: Primary EMPEROR-Preserved randomized trial report; one study cohort.

cases.title: Effectiveness of immune checkpoint inhibitors and other treatment modalities in patients with advanced mucosal melanomas: a systematic review and individual patient data meta-analysis
cases.record_status: PubMed record identity confirmed; publication type field was not available in the captured record and remains unassigned.
cases.population: Patients with locally advanced or metastatic mucosal melanoma included in eligible cohort and observational studies.
cases.total_n_sentence: From a total of 7402 studies, 35 eligible studies comprising a total of 2833 participants were included.

outcomes.outcome: 12-month overall survival for combined anti-PD1 and anti-CTLA4
outcomes.source_sentence: Combined anti-PD1 and anti-CTLA4 therapy had the highest 12-month OS and 12-month PFS at 71.8% (95% CI: 67.6%, 76.2%, n = 476) and 35.1% (95% CI: 30.5%, 40.4%, n = 401) respectively

outcomes.outcome: 12-month progression-free survival for combined anti-PD1 and anti-CTLA4
outcomes.source_sentence: Combined anti-PD1 and anti-CTLA4 therapy had the highest 12-month OS and 12-month PFS at 71.8% (95% CI: 67.6%, 76.2%, n = 476) and 35.1% (95% CI: 30.5%, 40.4%, n = 401) respectively

outcomes.outcome: overall survival, anti-PD1 plus anti-CTLA4 versus anti-PD1 alone
outcomes.source_sentence: In the double-arm studies, combination therapy with anti-PD1 and anti-CTLA4 had similar OS and PFS with anti-PD1 alone (OS: HR 0.856 (95% CI: 0.704, 1.04); RMTL ratio 0.932 (95% CI: 0.832, 1.044, P = 0.225); RMST ratio 1.102 (95% CI: 0.948, 1.281, P = 0.204); PFS: HR 0.919 (95% CI: 0.788, 1.07); RMTL ratio 0.936 (95% CI: 0.866, 1.013, P = 0.100); RMST ratio 1.21 (95% CI: 0.979, 1.496, P = 0.078))

cases.study_relationship: Systematic review and IPD meta-analysis of 35 included studies; 2833 participants are pooled data, not a new primary cohort. Subgroup n values (476, 401, etc.) must not be mistaken for total N.

cases.title: Course and prognosis of adult-onset epilepsy in Brazil: A cohort study.
cases.record_status: PubMed PMID/title/DOI, publication type, and abstract confirmed.
cases.population: 302 individuals with adult-onset epilepsy followed in a University Hospital in Brazil.
cases.total_n_sentence: We followed 302 individuals with adult-onset epilepsy for 9.8 years in our University Hospital.

outcomes.source_sentence: Overall 47 (15.6%) individuals presented drug-resistant epilepsy and the etiology was structural in 70.2% of them, while infectious etiology was present in 8.5% of this group.

outcomes.outcome: seizures in individuals with developmental delay
outcomes.source_sentence: Those with developmental delay were two times more likely to present seizures.

cases.study_relationship: Primary longitudinal cohort report; 302 individuals, 9.8-year follow-up.

cases.title: Prior antibiotics and risk of antibiotic-resistant community-acquired urinary tract infection: a case-control study
cases.record_status: PubMed record confirms title/DOI/abstract; case-control design is explicit in the article title and abstract, while publication-type field itself does not list that design.
cases.population: Patients with symptomatic UTI and laboratory-proven E. coli infection in 10 UK general practices; cases had resistant infection and controls susceptible infection.
cases.total_n_sentence: Risk of ampicillin-resistant E. coli infection in 903 patients was associated with amoxicillin prescriptions of >or=7 days duration in the previous 1 month [odds ratio (OR)=3.91, 95% CI 1.64-9.34] and previous 2-3 months (2.29, 1.12-4.70) before illness onset.

outcomes.outcome: ampicillin-resistant E. coli infection and prior amoxicillin exposure >=7 days in previous month
outcomes.source_sentence: Risk of ampicillin-resistant E. coli infection in 903 patients was associated with amoxicillin prescriptions of >or=7 days duration in the previous 1 month [odds ratio (OR)=3.91, 95% CI 1.64-9.34] and previous 2-3 months (2.29, 1.12-4.70) before illness onset.

outcomes.outcome: trimethoprim-resistant E. coli infection and prior trimethoprim exposure >=7 days
outcomes.source_sentence: For trimethoprim-resistant E. coli infections, the OR was 8.44 (3.12-22.86) for prescriptions of trimethoprim of >or=7 days in the previous month and 13.91 (3.32-58.31) for the previous 2-3 months.

cases.study_relationship: Primary case-control report; association estimates do not establish treatment causality.

cases.title: Diagnosis of thyroid disease in hospitalized patients: a systematic review.
cases.record_status: PubMed PMID/title/DOI, publication types, and abstract confirmed.
cases.population: Hospitalized inpatients; general medical, geriatric, or psychiatric inpatient populations are discussed.

outcomes.outcome: prevalence of thyroid disease among inpatients
outcomes.source_sentence: Prevalence of thyroid disease among inpatients is approximately 1% to 2% and is similar to the outpatient population.

outcomes.outcome: positive likelihood ratio for abnormal sTSH in ill inpatients vs outpatients
outcomes.source_sentence: The positive likelihood ratio associated with an abnormal sTSH test result in ill inpatients is about 10 compared with about 100 in outpatients.

cases.study_relationship: Systematic review; no new cohort or pooled participant total is reported in the abstract.

cases.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Primary Care Clinicians Across a Statewide System of Autism Evaluation
cases.record_status: PubMed PMID/title/DOI, abstract, and listed publication types confirmed.
cases.population: Children aged 14 to 48 months referred for expert follow-up evaluation.
cases.total_n_sentence: Among 126 children (mean age: 2.6 years; 77% male; 14% Latinx; 66% non-Latinx white), 82% (n = 103) had consistent ASD outcomes between the index and reference evaluation.

outcomes.source_sentence: Sensitivity was 81.5%, specificity was 82.4%, positive predictive value was 92.6%, and negative predictive value was 62.2%.
Sensitivity was 81.5%, specificity was 82.4%, positive predictive value was 92.6%, and negative predictive value was 62.2%.

cases.study_relationship: Primary prospective diagnostic accuracy study; n=103 agreement subset is not total sample size; AUC and confidence intervals are not reported in the abstract.

cases.title: Eagle syndrome presentation and outcomes in a large surgical case series
cases.record_status: PubMed PMID/title/DOI and complete abstract confirmed; publication-types field not exposed in the captured record.
cases.population: 56 adults with Eagle syndrome at a tertiary center; all operations by one surgeon.
cases.total_n_sentence: This retrospective case series included 56 patients at least 18 years of age or older with a diagnosis of Eagle syndrome.

arms.label: surgical treatment
arms.intervention: surgical treatment; 92.2% intraoral and 7.8% cervical approaches

outcomes.outcome: patient-reported symptom resolution or improvement after surgery
outcomes.source_sentence: All patients (100%) reached in a phone survey stated that their symptoms resolved or improved after surgery.

cases.study_relationship: Primary retrospective case series; report does not state phone-survey respondent count, so no denominator may be inferred.

cases.title: Thoracic Outlet Syndrome: Diagnostic Accuracy of MRI.
cases.record_status: PubMed PMID/title/DOI, publication type and abstract confirmed; abstract defines intra-operative findings as reference standard.
cases.population: 48 patients who underwent surgery for thoracic outlet syndrome after work-up including MRI.
cases.total_n_sentence: We retrospectively included 48 patients who underwent surgery for TOS after a work-up that included MRI (1.5-T, n=29 and 3-T, n=19).

outcomes.source_sentence: For diagnosing a cervical rib, MRI had 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity.
For diagnosing a cervical rib, MRI had 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity.

cases.study_relationship: Primary retrospective diagnostic cohort; 1.5-T and 3-T are imaging subgroups within n=48 and must not be counted as independent cohorts.
